answer.summary: Bier says founders often mistake a tactic he used to test adoption at individual schools for the app’s ongoing growth strategy: following every student at school after school. It helped recruit the first 100 users and test product density; the app was meant to grow on its own afterward.

sections.heading: The mistaken assumption
sections.content: Founders often think Bier grew the app by going school to school and following every student. He clarifies that this was how they tested apps, not how the app itself grew; doing it at many schools is unrealistic.

sections.heading: What the tactic was for
sections.content: They used dedicated school Instagram accounts to reach students whose bios identified their school, aiming to create enough adoption density for a social network’s flywheel to start. They manually got the first 100 users this way to assess whether the product worked and whether students reached the aha moment; after that, the app should grow by itself.
